title: The Face Taking Shape
logline: A sculptor has spent three weeks on the eyes of a Buddha image and still isn't satisfied. He won't say what he's looking for, only that he'll know it when the face stops looking back.

object.note: Object 6 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From a community holding one member in mind to a sculptor holding one face in mind, in detail, for weeks.

thread_out.thread: The patient attention given to a carved face becomes care given to living ones: a mother's single day moving between children who each need something different.

lesson.in_simple_terms: One old way of building faith is to look at a Buddha image so carefully, from head to feet, that it can be seen with eyes closed. The texts say that when the mind is full of good qualities like this, it settles and turns glad and calm.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: බුදු රුවක් හිසේ සිට පාදය දක්වා සැලකිල්ලෙන් බලා ඇස් පියාගෙන වුවද දැකිය හැකි තරමට සිතට ගැනීම බුදුගුණ සිහි කිරීමේ එක් ක්‍රමයක් වන අතර, එවිට සිත සන්සුන්ව සතුටින් පිරෙන බව පොත්වල දැක්වේ.
lesson.the_teaching: Recollection of the Buddha is a calm-meditation practice. The Margaya gives two ways in: looking at a beloved Buddha image part by part, from head to feet, until it is drawn in the mind, or dwelling on a few qualities one genuinely understands; it insists that reciting memorised lines one does not understand is not this practice. The Pradeepika says that as the qualities are recollected the mind is not pressed by greed, hatred or delusion, it straightens, and joy, calm, ease and steadiness follow. Among the beautiful factors, faith is described as a clarifying confidence, like a gem that settles the mud in water.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film watches the sculptor's long, silent attention to one feature at a time, the checking of proportions, and the refusal to say what is being looked for. The viewer sees attention held with meaning rather than repetition, and the moment the eyes are finished, when the face 'stops looking back', becomes the turn.

key_terms.en: tranquillity; calming of bodily and mental strain

lesson.caution: This does not mean any long, careful looking is this meditation; the texts describe a devotional support aimed at recollecting the Buddha himself, not a general visualisation technique for wellbeing.
lesson.builds_on: The mutual-aid society held one member in mind; this film narrows that to one person holding one face in mind, in detail, for weeks, and shows faith as something practised.
